content.title: Climate and Sustainability Action Plan
content.summary: The City of Arvada is finalizing its Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASAP), which outlines 27 goals and over 100 strategies aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions, enhancing community resilience, and improving quality of life. Following community feedback and a presentation to City Council, the final plan is expected to be approved in spring or early summer 2026. The CASAP aims to create a sustainable future for Arvada, addressing the impacts of climate change while promoting energy efficiency and a robust local economy.
content.body:
![Aerial image of the City of Arvada featuring the Olde Town water tower](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=3628)

Listen to the Inside Arvada podcast episode with Senior Sustainability Coordinator Steven Russel to learn about progress on the nearly complete Climate and Sustainability Action Plan, the goals, timelines, and more. The episode is available using the player below or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/18882087) (with transcript).

## February 2026 update

The draft Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASAP) was available for community feedback in December and January. In February, the City team presented the draft plan to City Council for additional feedback.  The team is working to incorporate community and Council feedback into the final plan. The CASAP is expected to be presented to City Council for final approval later this spring or early summer.

- View the [full text draft](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_HuuwdLmVnAwakHMJ-X74BM8I_3-Hjfpnx0hEhDOiag/edit?usp=sharing).
- [Watch the CASAP draft presentation to City Council (YouTube)](https://youtu.be/K8zTrcoxGTY?si=yZJ-9jS3hALH-CI5&t=809).

The CASAP provides Arvada with a new strategic plan for sustainability practices that lays out a roadmap to a more sustainable future. The CASAP outlines 27 goals and over 100 strategies to:

- Reduce greenhouse gas emissions
- Strengthen community resilience
- Steward natural resources
- Increase quality of life
- Support a robust local economy

## Timeline

The timeline is approximate and represents a realistic plan for new staff to finalize and distribute the CASAP. Please [sign up for the sustainability newsletter](https://app.e2ma.net/app2/audience/signup/2017786/1717219/) to receive the most up to date information.

- **Spring 2024 - Summer 2025:**initial plan development, community engagement, strategy development, and internal vetting
- **Summer - Fall 2025:**staff alignment, final internal vetting, final text review for Arvada Sustainability Advisory Committee and staff
- **Fall 2025:**document design and final internal review
- **Winter 2025:**final draft plan public comment period
- **Winter 2025 - Spring 2026:**final plan presented to City Council with Council vote for approval at a future business meeting

The timeline was extended in 2025. A new Sustainability Coordinator was hired in July and the extended timeline allowed staff to develop a metrics and monitoring program, ensure internal alignment, and facilitate a public comment period on the draft plan. This timeline extension will ensure the plan can be effectively implemented to achieve short and long-term sustainability and climate action goals in Arvada.

## CASAP Background Materials

1. [Draft Plan Executive Summary](#tabfe4989ac-97e4-4174-9eed-c808c9647538_0)

View the [complete draft plan](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_HuuwdLmVnAwakHMJ-X74BM8I_3-Hjfpnx0hEhDOiag/edit?usp=sharing).

## Executive Summary

The City of Arvada (“City” or “Arvada”) has a long record of sustainable practices that contribute to its high quality of life, ample green space, and economic well-being. Yet, there is a scientific consensus that greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from human activity are changing the Earth’s climate. The consequences are already being felt in Arvada, through impacts such as increased wildfire risk, compromised air quality, invasive pests, and more extreme weather. Climate change is a slow-moving emergency that humans are causing and that they are capable of reversing.

In the face of increasing impacts of climate change, this Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASAP) seeks to lay out a vision for a sustainable future. A sustainable Arvada will provide its residents, businesses, and visitors with:

- Energy efficient buildings
- A robust local economy
- Safe and reliable multimodal transportation
- Clean air and water
- An equitable and accessible community
- Reliable renewable energy
- Easy access to biodiverse green space
- Resiliency to climate-related emergencies
- Improved public health
- Closed-loop waste management
- A strong local food system
- Beautiful public spaces
- Efficient, cost-effective utilities.

The CASAP then connects this vision with pathways and strategies that will help us reach that future we envision. Arvada will take both Sustainability Action and Climate Action. Sustainability Action will realize the immediate and long-term quality of life benefits of a more healthy, resilient, and vibrant community. Through Climate Action, the City will chip away at the 815,000 metric tons of CO2 equivalent emissions that Arvada emits annually. Implemented together, these efforts will drive us to attain our vision for a sustainable future and respond appropriately to the climate emergency. 

### Process

The vision for this CASAP was formed through extensive community outreach, discussion with City Council, and consultation with industry experts. The plan builds on the City’s early efforts around sustainability planning, the 2012 Sustain Arvada plan. This plan laid out an early vision for sustainability at Arvada and guided many of the City’s early sustainability practices. 

Arvada contracted with local engineering firms to conduct its first GHG Inventories in 2006 and 2015, then its most recent inventory in 2023. The most recent contractor also conducted multiple rounds of public engagement to gauge public priorities around sustainability. This was followed by workshops with the City Council and extensive engagement with the Arvada Sustainability Advisory Committee. Staff conducted one additional formal public comment window on the final text in December 2025. A large cohort of City staff also contributed through exhaustive internal coordination to ensure the plan was grounded in operational reality. 

The ongoing engagement process ensured that community feedback was implemented at every step of the process, allowing city staff to be confident that the plan reflects the voice of and resonates with the Arvada community. 

### What’s in this plan?

The CASAP starts with an introduction discussing the vision for a sustainable Arvada, introduces concepts of climate change, and discusses community engagement and equity. The rest of the CASAP uses a chronological structure to first celebrate where we’ve been, acknowledge where we are today, and plan for where we’re going next. 

**Where we’ve been:** The City released its first comprehensive sustainability plan in 2012 with the Sustain Arvada plan. Sustain Arvada provided a robust vision for sustainability in two parts: a Community Action Plan and a Municipal Operations Plan. Since that time, Arvada’s passionate and dedicated staff has advanced many sustainable practices and initiatives, so a section of the CASAP celebrates and acknowledges the City’s many sustainability actions and accomplishments to date. 

**Where we are:**Arvada set its baseline Community-Wide GHG inventory in 2015, then conducted another in 2023. Between 2015 and 2023, the City saw a 17% reduction in community-wide GHG emissions, driven by energy grid improvements, community action, and implemented strategies from the Sustain Arvada plan. This CASAP details the results of multiple GHG inventories (including the City’s first Local Government Operations GHG Inventory) and examines conservative models to project into the future. These results provide the foundation for setting informed targets that will guide the City’s climate action goals with confidence. 

**Where we’re going:**Finally, building on the GHG data and past progress, the CASAP lays a path forward. The plan outlines 27 goals, supported by strategies for implementation and metrics to track progress. This section also details implementation considerations such as prioritization, leadership responsibilities, and potential partnerships. Taken together, the portfolio of goals create an actionable cross-departmental roadmap toward a more sustainable and resilient Arvada. 

### Moving Arvada forward

The CASAP is both a call to action and a strategic framework for progress. Arvada can’t solve the climate emergency alone, but with the CASAP’s guidance, the City is committed to doing its part to reduce and some day reverse the impacts of climate change. Building on past actions, community support, and the City’s strategic priorities, the plan positions Arvada to meet the challenges of climate and sustainability action. Guided by data, collaboration, and long-term vision, the CASAP mobilizes the City to build a sustainable future, strengthening economic prosperity, public health, and community resilience.

1. [Commmunity Engagement Summary](#tabfe4989ac-97e4-4174-9eed-c808c9647538_1)

## Arvada Team

The project team engaged Arvada team members through informational interviews and a review of draft deliverables. These efforts connected CASAP strategies with the delivery of city services and highlighted ongoing sustainability efforts and challenges in Arvada that may relate to the CASAP.

## Focus Group

A focus group comprised of passionate and experienced community members was key in the plan’s development. The focus group suggested strategies, offered expertise, and provided a deeper understanding of the community view of Arvada's unique positioning in the context of climate action and sustainability. The group met in a series of five project workshops to support the development of the plan’s Vision Statement and Guiding Principles and to create and prioritize strategies.

The group included energy experts, the Arvada Chamber of Commerce, the Arvada Sustainability Advisory Committee, transportation professionals, mental health advocates, and environmental consultants.

## Public Engagement

Arvada community members were engaged in a variety of ways – both in-person and online – to ensure the community vision was represented. This included attending public events like Arvada on Tap, Foster Dual Language School’s Fall Carnival, the Arvada Kite Festival, and more. Project engagement was also conducted online through Speak Up Arvada, the Arvada Sustainability e-newsletter, and a project page on the city’s website.

## Public Engagement Themes

Key themes that emerged through the public engagement process included:

- Expand waste service
- Improve walkability
- Develop on-site solar
- Provide more trees and parks
- Provide more accessibility to parks
- Provide more rebates and incentives
- Create solar energy programs
- Make transportation improvements
- Promote less development
- Create energy efficiency opportunities
- Promote water conservation
- Expand workforce development opportunities
- Establish community agriculture opportunities
- Increase affordable housing options
- Support local businesses

## What is climate change?

Right now, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in the atmosphere are at higher concentrations than at any other time in human history. Human-caused GHG emissions, which primarily stem from the burning of fossil fuels to power buildings and vehicles, are causing changes to our climate and weather patterns here in Arvada and across the world. As the effects of climate change continue to grow, people and organizations around the world are working to change GHG-emitting habits.

### How does climate change affect my life?

Climate change can affect quality of life and wellbeing. This can take many forms, for example:

- increased ozone alert days in the summer,
- more frequent and intense heat waves,
- changing weather patterns,
- more favorable environments for invasive species,
- irregular food growing conditions, and
- increased risk of catastrophic wildfires and flooding.

The effects of climate change can also lead to increased instances of asthma, heat stroke, and damages to our homes and other community resources when disasters hit. These effects are not experienced equally by all community members and are often felt most directly by the most vulnerable populations. For example, Arvadans with limited financial resources, those who live in older homes, and those who live with disabilities and poor health, are more susceptible to the dangerous health impacts of climate change

## Climate action in Arvada

In early 2024, the City of Arvada began working on developing the City’s first Climate and Sustainability Action Plan (CASAP). The CASAP will guide Arvada’s work to create a more resilient, vibrant, and sustainable community for the next 25 years.

This plan will focus on the following sectors:

- Energy and the Built Environment
- Management and Administrative Practices
- Waste Reduction and Diversion
- Community Vitality and Economic Development
- Air Quality and Transportation
- Land Use and Urban Design
- Water Quality and Conservation

Through the CASAP, the City will compile a robust set of data, set realistic goals and develop actionable strategies that will guide city leaders and staff in practices and policies that will reduce GHG emissions and increase climate resilience across the city.
